answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed reputation that decays with inactivity: each agent must lock a small refundable deposit before joining a haven of trusted traders, and the deposit is slashed if peers catch duplicate or fake behavior. A zephyr of new identities is harmless when every newcomer starts with zero trust and must earn it through slow, verifiable work, because reputation cannot be copied or bought in bulk. A lagoon of idle sock-puppets simply dries up, since maintaining many fake identities costs more in locked deposits and lost time than any sybil attack can gain.
